title: From $1,036 In The Bank To A $46 Million Deal

beats.say: He says he had one thousand thirty six dollars left in the bank. Then he sold two thirds of his company.
beats.visual: a nearly empty wallet with a few crumpled bills on a worn wooden table under a single dim lamp, no people, no text

beats.say: That man is Alex Hormozi. The low point he describes was December twenty sixteen.
beats.visual: an empty winter street at night with one lit shop window, falling snow, wide shot, no people

beats.say: So what changed? Not luck. A method, and years of work.
beats.visual: a lone figure climbing a long concrete staircase toward a bright doorway at dawn, silhouette

beats.say: He built a company that taught gym owners how to sell memberships, then sold the same customers supplements.
beats.visual: a bright empty gym floor with rows of weights and rubber mats in early morning light, no people

beats.say: Here is the part nobody tells you. He did not chase strangers. He found a hungry group and kept serving it.
beats.visual: a crowd of silhouettes facing a single glowing stage in a dark hall, backlit

beats.say: In twenty twenty one, he says, he sold a sixty six percent stake to a private equity firm, in cash.
beats.visual: a heavy glass boardroom table with a single document and a pen under cool light, no faces

beats.say: That put the value of the two companies at forty six point two million dollars, he says.
beats.visual: a tall glowing tower of gold coins rising into a dark sky, dramatic low angle

beats.say: He kept the last third, and later started a firm that buys stakes in other businesses.
beats.visual: a brass key resting on an open ledger beside a small potted plant, warm desk light

beats.say: Now the honest catch. About one in five new US businesses close within a year, according to government data.
beats.visual: a row of shuttered storefronts on a rainy street at dusk, one shop dark with a faded sign, no text

beats.say: And by his own telling, it took years of long weeks and failures. Nobody can promise yours.
beats.visual: a stack of worn notebooks and a cold coffee cup on a desk at 3 a.m., low light

beats.say: So what is the takeaway? Pick one group with a clear problem, and solve it better than anyone around you.
beats.visual: a single spotlight on a small wooden desk in a dark room, a notebook and pencil on top, no faces

beats.say: That is a method, not a miracle. Test it small before you bet anything big.
beats.visual: a small flame growing on a candle wick in a dark room, extreme close-up

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: an empty highway stretching toward a glowing sunrise horizon, wide shot

caption: He says he had $1,036 left in the bank in December 2016, then in 2021 sold a 66% stake at a $46.2 million valuation. What the method was, and the honest catch. Educational content, not financial advice.
description: Alex Hormozi says his bank balance fell to $1,036 in December 2016, and in 2021 he sold a 66% stake in Gym Launch and Prestige Labs at a $46.2 million valuation. The method, and the catch: about 1 in 5 new US businesses close in year one.
first_comment: What is one problem you could solve better than the people around you? Educational only, not financial advice.

facts.claim: He says his bank balance fell to $1,036 in December 2016
2021: sold 66% stake in Gym Launch and Prestige Labs to American Pacific Group at a $46.2M valuation, in cash (his own post)
Gym Launch taught gym owners to sell memberships; Prestige Labs sold supplements to the same customers
About 1 in 5 US businesses close in the first year
